note: Structured version of study-content/SOURCE-ISSUES.md plus app-specific extraction notes, so each item links to the exact PDF pages. Wording summarizes the pack; it is not instructor text.

items.title: Chapter outline labels differ from the lecture sequence
items.detail: The August 24 outline labels Chapter 4 “Bivariate distributions”, but the September 28–October 5 lectures cover continuous univariate distributions in Chapter 4. It also labels a regression entry “Chapter 9” while citing Chapter 11 sections. Lessons follow the actual lecture sequence; regression is treated as a Chapter 11 preview.

items.title: Stem-and-leaf display has 34 leaves; frequency table has 35 observations
items.detail: The developed stem display on p. 4 lists 34 leaves, while the histogram table lists 35 observations including one in [0.07,0.08); stem row 07 is blank. Each display is used as given; no missing leaf is invented. Page 3 is explicitly schematic.

items.title: Outlier fences are inclusive (course convention)
items.detail: The notes use “at least” 1.5 IQR and classify a value exactly on the lower inner fence as a mild outlier. Quizzes honour equality rather than the strict inequality used by much software.

items.title: Textbook stem-and-leaf plot for Site I flagged in the notes
items.detail: The notes flag an error in a textbook stem-and-leaf plot and suggest confirming its ordering/key with the instructor. The 23-value ordered list in the notes is internally usable; the textbook itself was not supplied.

items.title: Five-number summary: actual extremes vs whisker endpoints
items.detail: The September 2 review writes {P1, Q1, Q2, Q3, P2} with whisker endpoints. The August 31 definition and worked examples use the actual minimum and maximum (p. 5 uses an outlier as the minimum). Lessons and quizzes use the actual extremes.

items.title: Probability zero vs impossibility
items.detail: The finite examples equate probability zero with impossibility. In general (e.g. continuous variables) a singleton has probability zero without being impossible; probability one means almost sure.

items.title: “Almost all within three standard deviations” is informal
items.detail: Early notes use informal three-standard-deviation language. It is not a universal 99.7% claim: October 5 distinguishes Chebyshev's bound from the normal empirical rule.

items.title: Intermediate arithmetic in a definite integral
items.detail: The final probability 0.1875 is correct, but the printed intermediate values −0.1875 and −0.375 are not the values of 6.25x² − 1.25x at 0.3 and 0.2 (correct: 0.1875 and 0). The CDF calculation on p. 6 agrees with 0.1875.

items.title: Covariance unit-conversion illustration
items.detail: The illustration changes covariance 12.51 to 0.36 for a Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion. If both variables convert by F = (9/5)C + 32, covariance scales by (9/5)², giving 40.5324. The October 12 centimeter-to-inch example applies the rule correctly. The questionable numbers are not reproduced.

items.title: Weak/moderate/strong correlation labels are classroom heuristics
items.detail: The strength cutoffs are classroom guides, not universal standards. R measures linear association; the R² interpretation assumes simple least squares with an intercept.

items.title: Method of moments and MLE are introduction only
items.detail: Both methods are named, but no procedure is worked through. The general preference statement does not prove every MLE has smaller bias or variance. Not treated as covered material.

items.title: Finishing-time sample-mean calculation is an authored extension
items.detail: The notes end after specifying the individual model N(61, 81). The sample-of-nine calculation in lesson 20 and related practice are authored extensions.

items.title: Sections 2.4 and 3.9 are explicitly skipped
items.detail: September 16 says to skip Section 2.4 and September 23 skips Section 3.9. They are not presented as covered.

items.title: Later syllabus material is not in the supplied notes
items.detail: The syllabus plans Chapters 8 and 11 and a comprehensive final. The notes (through October 14) do not develop confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, a central limit theorem, or full regression. This app covers the supplied notes only.

items.title: Assigned textbook exercises are referenced but not supplied
items.detail: The notes cite textbook exercise numbers, but the textbook and homework solution files are not in this folder. Those prompts were not reconstructed; all practice questions in this app are newly authored.

items.title: Extracted PDF text alters mathematical glyphs
items.detail: Search snippets come from text extracted from the PDFs. Math italic letters, fractions, overbars (x̄ appears as “¯x”), and subscripts may be garbled or split across lines. Lessons use authored LaTeX; open the PDF page for the instructor's exact notation. Only selected pages were visually inspected by the content pack.
